svg.title: P010 · Headline order KPIs
svg.desc: One summary row for all orders. Order IDs 1, 2, 3 give three orders. Customer IDs 10, 10, 20 give two distinct buyers. 100 + 200 + 300 = 600. All three amounts are known, so 600 / 3 = 200 per order. The earliest order is January 1 and the latest is January 3. All six metrics describe the same three orders. FROM Orders · one table is enough. Each transaction contributes once to the headline figures. Its order ID, buyer ID, amount and date supply all six measures. Buyer 10 can therefore have two orders while counting as one buyer.
svg.text: One summary row for all orders.
Three orders belong to two people. Which headline numbers should be 3 and 2?
A triangle marks an example to follow. A dark source band spans its columns. ƒ marks a calculated value. Deeper cell colors mark the values to
follow. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.
What makes an order different from a buyer?

g.aria-label: FROM Orders · one table is enough
g.text: FROM Orders · one table is enough
Each transaction contributes once to the headline figures. Its order ID, buyer ID, amount and date supply all six
measures. Buyer 10 can therefore have two orders while counting as one buyer.

svg.text: Order IDs 1, 2, 3 give three orders. Customer IDs 10, 10, 20 give two distinct buyers.
Which values feed revenue and average order value?
100 + 200 + 300 = 600. All three amounts are known, so 600 / 3 = 200 per order.
What period do these figures cover?
The earliest order is January 1 and the latest is January 3. All six metrics describe the same three orders.
